text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Gerhard Praschak, the former chief executive of Kontrollbank who committed suicide over the weekend, left behind letters and notes in which he blames undue poltical influence in the country's banking sector for his move.
- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel says he stands by a speech he held at NATO headquarters in Brussels in which he asked for a formal invitation to Austria to join the military alliance.

- The foreign ministry says it does not plan to investigate its involvement in the affair around the release of the alleged murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989, while both the interior ministry and the justice ministry say they want to prepare reports for a special parliamentary session on May 6.
- Insurer EA-Generali says it plans to continue its close cooperation with savings bank Die Erste (First Austrian).

- As many as 41 percent of Austrians fear the introduction of Europe's ingle currency euro will have a negative effect on their future, blaming the government's austerity measures and possible job cuts.
- Bank GiroCredit plans to open subsidiaries in Mexico and Chile.
- Rubber goods maker Semperit wants to expand in South East Asia. A 33 million schillings capital increase is planned in June.
DIE PRESSE
- The government said it would not follow the demands of a popular referendum earlier this month which called for a ban of genetically modified foods.
- Hannes Swoboda, Social Democrat Member of the European Parliament, says his party should continue its internal debate on Austria's future security policy.
- Consumer prices rose just 1.5 percent in March, after an increase of 1.8 percent in February.
- The government audit office has criticised former Austria Tabak chief Beppo Mauhart for granting subsidies to sporting goods maker HTM, then a unit of Austria Tabak, of some 1.6 billion schillings.
- Bank GiroCredit's operating profit rose to 2.1 billion schillings in 1996 from 1.9 billion schillings a year earlier.
- Austria's sole motorbike maker KTM reports first half sales up 23 percent. The company says it now eyes expansion.
- Saudi or South African companies are likely to finance a major railway tunnel project in eastern Austria.
KURIER
- Claus Raidl, chief executive of steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm, says the survival of Vienna's stock exchange is in the hands of investors.
- Insurer EA-Generali wants to take over postal savings bank PSK even if postal and telecoms monopoly PTA would retain a stake in PSK.
- Regional bank Hypo Kaernten plans to expand in southern Europe and the capital Vienna, after reporting a 50 percent jump in 1996 earnings.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Motorbike maker KTM says it has plans to be listed at the New York Stock Exchange.
